title: Isolation-based Spherical Ensemble Representations for Tabular Anomaly Detection
summary: The paper addresses unsupervised tabular anomaly detection, where methods must catch global, local, and dependency anomalies without distributional assumptions while staying scalable. ISER samples t random partitions of ψ points, builds hyperspheres whose radii are nearest-neighbor distances within each sampled subset, represents each point as φ = 1 − 1/r of the smallest covering sphere (φ = 1 if uncovered) concatenated across partitions, and scores points either by averaging (ISER-A) or by cosine similarity to the all-ones anomaly reference vector (ISER-S); ISER-IF additionally runs iForest on the transformed representation Φ(x) with an inverted path-length score. Across 20 PyOD/ODDS benchmark datasets, ISER-S achieves the best average AUC-ROC of 0.8523 versus 12 baselines, and ISER-IF improves iForest on Ionosphere from 0.8530 to 0.9314 (+9.19%).

match_target.why: The user hint names Table IV, ISER-IF AUC-ROC on Ionosphere (0.9314). It is the cheapest run in the paper (351x32 data, CPU seconds, no training tricks) and directly demonstrates a headline contribution (ISER-IF lifting iForest by 9.19%), not a side ablation.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: the target is a bounded score (AUC-ROC) printed in [0,1] on a small set (Ionosphere has 351 examples, so rule 2's 2,000+ threshold does not apply). The paper reports no std (only 'Each experiment is repeated 5 times and reported average results'), so rule 1 does not apply. Band = 0.02 absolute around 0.9314, i.e. reproduced AUC in [0.9114, 0.9514].

requirements.stmt: Build t partitionings; in each, randomly sample psi points from D without replacement as hypersphere centers (Algorithm 1).
requirements.quote: Randomly sample ψ points from D without replacement

requirements.stmt: Each hypersphere's radius equals the distance from its center to its nearest neighbor within the sampled subset Di (not random pairs as in ADERH).
requirements.quote: each hypersphere's radius is determined by the distance to each sample point's nearest neighbor within the sampled subset

requirements.stmt: For each point x and partitioning, collect covering spheres Ci(x) and select the one with the smallest radius; phi_i(x) = 1 - 1/r of that sphere.
requirements.cite: Section III-A, equations for Ci(x), ẑi(x), phi_i(x)
requirements.quote: we select the covering hypersphere with the smallest radius

requirements.stmt: If x is covered by no hypersphere in a partitioning, set phi_i(x) = 1 (do not interpolate or clip; this is the local-anomaly mechanism).
requirements.cite: Section III-A, phi_i(x) definition; Remark IV.8
requirements.quote: φi(x) = 1, indicating that the point is not covered by any hyperspheres in this partitioning

requirements.stmt: Concatenate the t per-partitioning values into the ensemble representation Phi(x) in R^t.
requirements.quote: The ensemble representation of point x is constructed by concatenating the coverage indicators from all t partitionings

requirements.stmt: ISER-A score = arithmetic mean of the t components of Phi(x).
requirements.quote: The average-based anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean of all ensemble components

requirements.stmt: ISER-S score = cosine similarity between Phi(x) and the all-ones reference vector 1 = [1,...,1] in R^t.
requirements.quote: computed using cosine similarity between the point's ensemble representation and the anomaly reference vector

requirements.stmt: ISER-IF: fit standard iForest on the transformed features Phi(x) and use the modified (inverted) score S_ISER-IF(x, n) = 1 - 2^(-E(h(Phi(x)))/c(n)).
requirements.quote: we modify the original iForest anomaly scoring function [11] as:

requirements.stmt: The inversion must be implemented so that longer path lengths in the ISER feature space yield HIGHER anomaly scores (anomalies cluster tightly in Phi-space, normal points scatter).
requirements.cite: Section VI, paragraph after the inversion discussion
requirements.quote: shorter path lengths in the ISER feature space correspond to lower anomaly scores

requirements.stmt: Unsupervised contaminated setting: the method trains on the entire dataset including anomalies and is scored on the same data; AUC-ROC is the metric.
